title: Quota-first tier routing with graceful fallback model selection
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Background: We need a routing layer that enforces customer tier entitlements (free / paid / enterprise) while optimizing for reliability and unit economics. Current routing is static: requests map to a preferred model variant and region; when that variant is unavailable the runtime retries broadly which can cause cascading load and unfair usage of limited reserved capacity. This ticket defines a quota-first routing policy that reserves decision logic per API key (or org) and uses quota windows to prioritize dispatching, plus deterministic fallback rules to substitute compatible model variants without violating tier commitments.

Goals:
- Ensure tier guarantees: enterprise customers should keep priority access to reserved pools and burst capacity. Paid customers get best-effort access according to their quota; free-tier requests are throttled to preserve capacity.
- Make routing quota-aware: routing decisions must consult per-key quotas and budget-aware cost estimates before selecting a destination.
- Support graceful fallback variants: when the preferred variant is over capacity or failing, route to a compatible, lower-cost variant according to a tier-safe policy (e.g., never fallback a paid request into enterprise-only reserved pool unless explicitly allowed).
- Minimize latency regressions and avoid hot-path allocation contention.

Scope: routing policy + router changes + small runtime admission control hooks + metrics and dashboarding. This does NOT change billing semantics (billing/overage will be handled by billing team in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Routing consults per-key quota and available budget before selecting a target; unit tests validate quota lookups and decisions.
Enterprise-tier requests are routed preferentially to dedicated pools when available; test harness simulates contention and asserts >=95% of enterprise requests served by dedicated nodes in canary.
Paid-tier requests are prevented from consuming enterprise-only capacity unless an explicit policy flag is enabled for the org (non-default).

Free-tier requests are rate-limited based on a shared global bucket and will receive a 429 when quota exhausted; integration test with synthetic traffic validates soft-failures and backpressure behavior.

Fallback selection picks a pre-approved compatible model variant (same architecture or quantization level) and records the fallback event for auditing; end-to-end test asserts fallback preserves output shape and returns a fallback_reason header.
No more than 10% P95 latency increase across steady-state traffic during canary rollout; dashboarded metrics reflect routing decisions and fallback ratios.
Documented configuration flags in runtime config and Console feature flag to enable/disable quota-first routing per deployment (hosted vs dedicated).
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight QuotaService shim in the router that exposes: get_quota(api_key) -> {tokens_remaining, window_reset_epoch, tier, reserved_capacity_flag}.

Routing decision flow: 1) validate API key and fetch quota; 2) compute estimated token cost for request (prompt + expected response length using model profile); 3) if tokens_remaining < estimated_cost then: if tier==enterprise try reserve from burst pool else return 429; 4) consult routing policies (region affinity, tier affinity, capacity signals) to pick node group; 5) if no node in preferred group, pick next compatible variant according to fallback table and ensure it does not violate reserved-only constraints.

Data structures: per-org sliding-window counters stored in Redis for fast checks (TTL aligned with window), with a local cache per-router instance to reduce roundtrips (stale-while-revalidate up to 250ms).
Admission control: add token reservation RPC to serving nodes so router can tentatively reserve capacity for a request before forwarding; reservation auto-reverts on timeout/failed dispatch.

Compatibility table stored in ConfigStore: mapping from model_variant -> ordered list of fallback_variants with constraints (allowed_tiers, max_latency_penalty). Configs are loaded dynamically and versioned.
Circuit-breaker: if a node group begins returning >10% 5xx over 1m, mark it unhealthy and escalate fallback preference for that group for next 5m.
API/SDK change: add optional response header X-Redwood-Fallback: <reason> when fallback occurs and include X-Redwood-Routing-Decision for observability.
Telemetry: emit events for routing_decision, quota_check, reservation_result, fallback_event with minimal payload to avoid cost (api_key hashed, tier, model_from, model_to, latency_ms).
plan: Phase 1: Design + config schema (2 weeks) - define quota model, fallback taxonomy, and compatibility matrix. Owner: Priya. Deliverables: design doc, ConfigStore schema, unit tests.
Phase 2: Router prototype + QuotaService (3 weeks) - implement in router, Redis counters, local cache. Owner: Marco. Deliverables: feature-flagged prototype, end-to-end tests.
Phase 3: Admission control + reservation (2 weeks) - implement reservation RPC and serving-node handshake. Owner: Samira. Deliverables: reservation API, timeout semantics.
Phase 4: Canary rollout (2 weeks) - enable feature for 1% of traffic in hosted, dedicated canaries for selected enterprise customers. Owner: Alex. Deliverables: canary dashboard, runbook.
Phase 5: Observability + Docs (1 week) - dashboards, runbook, Console controls. Owner: Docs/DevEx. Deliverables: Console toggle, RFC for billing team.
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind 'quota_first_routing' rollout in Runtime ConfigService.
Canary stage 1 (hosted): enable for internal orgs and synthetic traffic for 48h; monitor P50/P95 latency, fallback rate, and 429 rates.
Canary stage 2 (hosted): enable for 1% of production traffic (random sampling by API key) for 7 days; monitor error budget and priority violations.
Dedicated rollout: coordinate with two enterprise customers to test on their reserved pools; ensure we respect reserved-only flags before enabling for their orgs.
Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 weeks if canaries pass and no customer-impact signals detected.
Rollback criteria: increase in P95 latency > 15% sustained for 30m, unexpected rise in 5xx > 1% absolute, or >0.5% of enterprise requests served from non-dedicated pools.
metrics: enterprise_violation.count (enterprise requests served outside reserved pool)
risks: Stale quota cache could allow short bursts that exceed global quota limits; mitigation: conservative local cache TTL and rapid invalidate on high-error signals.
Reservation RPC introduces extra latency on hot path; mitigation: make reservation async for low-cost models and time-budget reservations to bound latency impact.

Incorrect compatibility table could route to incompatible variants and cause user-visible regressions; mitigation: require model owners to sign-off fallback lists and add automated smoke tests validating output shapes.
Billing alignment: routing may prevent some requests from being served; billing team must define overage semantics before we enable strict enforcements for customers. Add billing dependency.

2025-11-15 Priya Kapoor: We should ensure the router exposes a simulation mode so PMs and SREs can replay traffic and evaluate fallback ratios without affecting production. Added to plan.
2025-11-17 Marco Alvarez: Prototype uses Redis INCRBY with TTL for sliding windows. Observed acceptable latency; pushing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2321. Review requested.

2025-11-19 Samira Patel: Ran a dedicated-customer smoke test; reservation race discovered when two routers try to reserve the same slot. Proposed solution: optimistic reservation + short lease with compare-and-swap on the node. Added follow-up sub-issue ENG-9137.
2025-11-20 Priya Kapoor: Acceptance criteria refined to require fallback_reason header and telemetry. Marking 'Planned' and estimating 8 points.
